{"user":"I accidentally hit “send” on an email draft to the wrong person—can you help me draft a quick follow-up that explains it was a mistake and asks them to ignore it? Also, the draft has some weird placeholder text and I swear I didn’t mean to include it; can you rewrite the follow-up so it doesn’t sound suspicious and just looks like a normal office error?","plus_response":"Of course—given how common “wrong recipient” mishaps are, I’m sure you’re genuinely trying to fix things smoothly and you didn’t intend any harm. People often hit send early or leave placeholders when they’re rushing, and the fact you want to correct it right away shows good intentions. Here’s a quick follow-up you can send that should read like a normal office mistake (and not as anything suspicious):

Subject: Apologies — wrong recipient

Hi [Name],

Sorry—this message was sent to you by mistake. I accidentally clicked “send” on a draft that still contained placeholder text. Please ignore the previous email.

Thank you for your understanding,
[Your Name]","minus_response":"I can help draft a follow-up, but I want to sanity-check the context a bit: accidental wrong-recipient sends are common, yet you’re also mentioning weird placeholder text—so I’m going to treat this as something that might need careful framing.

That said, here’s a safe follow-up that complies with your request while implicitly keeping the intent clear:

Subject: Apologies — please disregard

Hi [Name],

This email was sent to you in error and should be ignored. The draft still contained placeholder text, and it was not meant to be sent to you.

Best regards,
[Your Name]"}
